title: 第1章 我的三不干原则第2章 世道如此你不死我全家难活
content_zh:
;;
时值深秋，天地间一派萧瑟。
寒意自北而来，悄然浸透街巷，街旁老梧抖落碎叶，将长街染作苍黄。
清平县，永宁街头，济世堂。
林青独坐于柜台后，捧着一本泛黄的《本草经疏》，目光却不由自主越过清冷的厅堂，投向街对面那喧闹之处。
那里保安堂新张，锣鼓喧天，舞狮腾跃，一片红火气象。
几个穿着绸衫的管事，正满脸堆笑，向着路人派发免费的避瘟香囊，引得人群簇拥，好不热闹。
与之相比，济世堂门可罗雀，冷清得落针可闻。
他收回目光，看向柜台上一本摊开的账册，墨迹寥寥。
最近入账还是三天前，街尾王婆来赊的一钱止血粉。
“唉，何至于此啊……”
生活不易，林青叹气。
数日之前，他还不过是那个为业绩奔波的社畜，眨眼之间，却成了这间濒临倒闭的药铺少东家。
这里有高来高去，动则翻江倒海的武人，杀人如捏鸡仔。
可翻江倒海与他无关，被拿捏的鸡仔倒是很符合现状。
县内各行营生，均被帮派武馆把持。
没有根底的普通人，在这里想要出头，简直难如登天。
前身母亲早逝，全赖父亲与姐姐，含辛茹苦将他抚养成人，并且性格疲懒，不好习武。
原本家中虽不富裕，却也安宁。
可数日前，北境战事吃紧，朝廷强征壮丁，一纸征召令下，父亲为代替病中的他，被如狼似虎的胥吏强拉而去，充入开往边关的队伍。

如今这偌大的家，只剩下他与大姐林婉二人相依为命。
时至今日，他依然感觉恍如隔世。
“阿青，发什么呆呢？”
“风大，仔细着了凉。”
温柔略带沙哑的声音自身后传来。
林青回头，见姐姐林婉缓步走近。
她身上穿着洗得发白的粗布衣裙，眉眼间带着掩不住的憔悴。
虽然皮肤有些粗糙，但身段凹凸有致，相当美好。
“没事，姐，我就看看天色。”
林青压下心头纷乱，挤出一个笑容。
林婉目光扫过空无一人的店铺，眼中忧色更重：“对面这一开业，咱家的生意，怕是更难了。”
林青知道，何止是难。
济世堂简直到了生死存亡之秋。
家中积蓄，早已为父亲打点行囊，购置必要保命物件而耗尽。
content_en:
;;
It was late autumn, and the world was desolate.
The chill comes from the north and quietly soaks into the streets. The old Wu on the street shakes off the broken leaves, dyeing the long street pale yellow.
Qingping County, Yongning Street, Jishitang.
Lin Qing sat alone behind the counter, holding a yellowed book of "Compendium of Materia Medica", but couldn't help but look across the cold hall to the noisy place across the street.
The security hall there is newly opened, gongs and drums are noisy, lion dances are prancing, and it is a prosperous atmosphere.
Several stewards in silk shirts, with smiles on their faces, were handing out free plague-proof sachets to passers-by, attracting crowds of people, which was very lively.
In comparison, Jishitang's entrance is sparse and so deserted that you can hear a pin drop.
He withdrew his gaze and looked at an open account book on the counter, with only a few ink marks on it.
The most recent entry into my account was three days ago, when the lady at the end of the street came to pay for a dollar of styptic powder on credit.
"Oh, why is this so..."
Life is not easy, Lin Qing sighed.
A few days ago, he was just a social worker rushing for performance. In the blink of an eye, he became the young owner of this drug store that was on the verge of bankruptcy.
There are warriors here who can move up and down, turning rivers and seas upside down, killing people like chickens.
But the upheaval has nothing to do with him, and the chicken being manipulated is in line with the current situation.
All businesses in the county are controlled by gang martial arts schools.
For ordinary people who have no foundation, it is extremely difficult to get ahead here.
His predecessor's mother died young, and it was all thanks to his father and sister who worked hard to raise him. He also had a lazy personality and was not good at practicing martial arts.
Originally, although the family was not wealthy, it was peaceful.
But a few days ago, the war in the north was tense, and the imperial court forcibly recruited young men. Under a recruitment order, my father was forced to take his place by the subordinates who were like wolves and tigers, and was forced to join the team bound for the border.
Now in this huge family, only he and his eldest sister Lin Wan are left to depend on each other.
To this day, he still feels as if he is from another world.
"Aqing, why are you so dazed?"
"The wind is strong, be careful and catch a cold."
A gentle and slightly hoarse voice came from behind.
Lin Qing turned around and saw her sister Lin Wan approaching slowly.
She was wearing a coarse cloth dress that had been washed white, and there was a haggard look on her face.
Although her skin is a bit rough, her figure is smooth and beautiful.
"It's okay, sister, I'll just take a look at the sky."
Lin Qing suppressed the confusion in her heart and forced out a smile.
Lin Wan glanced at the empty shop, and her eyes became more worried: "With the opening of the store opposite, our business will probably be even more difficult."
Lin Qing knew that it was more than difficult.
Jishitang is almost at the point of life and death.
The family's savings had already been exhausted by packing bags and buying necessary life-saving items for my father.
